answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a staking garden: every identity must lock a slowly-maturing stake before gaining influence, like yarrow that takes a full season to root, so a hundred clones cannot fast-forward time. Voting weight then accrues only from attestations by distinct established peers, which leaves any hollow sockpuppet with no burned work and no history at zero weight no matter how many exist. One identity, one stake, one reputation trail: cheap to join honestly, expensive to fake at scale.
